faces.f: K'Ehleyr embraced the human tradition of using humor as a shield.
"The parasite appears to stimulate the victim's adrenal glands, generating great strength."
Federation shields are no match for Borg transporters.
"It's a time-honored way to practice medicine, with your head and your heart and your hands."
With implants and nanoprobes able to seal off systems and manufacture replacement parts, a Borg drone can endure damage that would be lethal to its constituent species.
"Where's your sense of adventure?"
"It'll be just like old times! Except different."
"Human intuition and instinct are not always right, but they do make life interesting."

"They've left behind their trivial, selfish lives, and they've been reborn with a greater purpose."
—The Borg Queen
Freed from the Collective, the great Klingon general Korok became its most fervent enemy.
The Borg quest for perfection cannot be purely technological. Organic offspring are grown from the strongest traits available.

"Spot, you are disrupting my ability to work."
—Lieutenant Commander Data
Every officer assimilated adds to the Collective's tactical genius.
The Borg ultimately seek perfection through unifying the strengths of all life-forms, whether those life-forms want perfection or not.
The Tholian's extreme life support requirements were no longer relevant post-assimilation.
Engineers on *Galaxy*-class ships might be able to replicate every spare part they need, but away from Federation supply lines, more ingenuity may be required.
The heart of every Borg vessel—the grit around which they form a geometrically perfect pearl—is a captured ship of at least passing technological interest.
"I am superior in many ways, but I would gladly give it up to be human."
"There's theory, and there's application. They don't always jibe."
"I feel as if all the boundaries within me are about to fall away."

"Imagine it: thousands of inhabited planets at our fingertips."
—Zefram Cochrane
The Borg had no notion of "quaint," but the simplicity of Federation technology was reassuring.
"I speak for the Borg."
"We are the future."
Nanoprobes subvert the will to the Collective even before the first implant is added.
With Picard's tactical knowledge guiding the Collective, the battle lasted only minutes. In the end, the Federation lost thirty-nine ships and eleven thousand souls.
Talaxian resilience and musculature provided the framework for excellent, and terrifying, labor drones.

"Knowledge lives on in the Collective as software. Components are repurposed for other drones. Not the file backup I'd prefer, but I suppose it is technically immortality."
—The Doctor
"A sharp knife is nothing without a sharp eye."
Ten years in the Cardassian camps couldn't break Ro's spirit. She wouldn't stop fighting just because the Federation asked politely.
It was a perfect match. Rom had the heart of a Bajoran and Leeta had the Ferengi flare for business.
"I suppose it's always going to be like this. Me against the Galaxy."

faces.f: "Hold on, even when you think you can't."
"I've discovered it's in joy that the uniqueness of each individual is revealed."
"Without trust, there's no friendship, no closeness, none of the emotional bonds that make us who we are."

"Brave words. I've heard them before, from thousands of species across thousands of worlds, since long before you were created."
—The Borg Queen
"We are Hugh."
"I assume a lecture on the futility of resistance is not going to be necessary."
"Why do you resist? We only wish to raise quality of life for all species."
The accidental assimilation of 29th-century technology created a unique drone, a collective of one.
A hero in his own mind.
"If you hear screams, consider that a request for a beam-out!"

"I am a Klingon! If you doubt it, a demonstration can be arranged!"

"Hard a-port! Bring us underneath for another volley!"
—Commander William Riker

"The Vulcans say that the desert teaches men the meaning of endurance, but it's the ice that forges real strength."
—Commander Shran, Andorian Imperial Guard
Transporters aren't always reliable, especially when you're coming in hot.

"I never thought size or strength was particularly important in a medical officer, but I can now say with certainty that they have their uses."
—Dr. Beverly Crusher

"The first duty of every Starfleet officer is to the truth, whether it's scientific truth, or historical truth, or personal truth. It is the guiding principle on which Starfleet is based."
—Captain Jean-Luc Picard
A good officer brings their best. A great officer brings out the best in their team.
"The true test of a warrior is not without. It is within."
"Away team to *Merrimack*. We're at the rendezvous, but Ensign Irvine hasn't checked in and won't reply on comms."
Their ability to replicate new circuits as they learn inadvertently bootstrapped exocomps into sentience in the 2360s.

"What thee are about to see comes down from the time of the beginning without change. This is the Vulcan heart; this is the Vulcan soul. This is our way."
—T'Pau
"Captain, the sensor sweep is fine, but my VISOR is picking up some disturbing fluctuations in the dilithium crystal matrix."
"Lanthanites live a long time, dear. It lets us learn all sorts of things, but you have to make your own fun."
"Humans needed the help of the Vulcans when they discovered warp drive. That need hasn't changed."
"Can I teach you a lesson?"
Ceti Alpha V's only remaining native life-form was a parasite who left hosts susceptible to suggestion.

"You play games with death, little warrior. I like it!"
—Captain Ma'ah
Beware a Klingon with a short temper and a big grudge.

Four thousand throats may be cut in one night by a running man.
—Klingon proverb
The Genesis Planet was dangerous. It provided Kruge with an amusing thrill.

"We Klingons have a reputation for ruthlessness. You will find that it is deserved."
—Commander Kor, military governor of Organia
Opponents write off Klingons as unthinking brutes at their own peril. When the Klingon Empire developed warp drive, humanity still relied on horse-drawn carts.
"I weary of the chase. Wait for me. I shall be merciful and quick."
Many sapient species hunt the ferocious gumato both for sport and the supposed medicinal benefits of its distinctive horn.

"Well, I had a choice. Do I walk away and let the emitter blow itself to hell? Or do I crawl in the Jefferies tube with twenty hook spiders?"
—Chief Miles O'Brien
The trusty disruptor pistol not only dissolves matter, but it's heavy enough to serve as a cudgel.
"That is what it is to be human: to make yourself more than you are."
"In critical moments, men sometimes see exactly what they wish to see."
"I've been looking in on the doings on your lively little Earth."
"Your life as it has been is over."
"I am the beginning, the end, the one who is many. I am the Borg."
"Risk is our business."
"If we're going to lose, then we're going to go down fighting, so that when our descendants someday rise up against the Dominion, they'll know what they're made of!"
"I am Tosk, the hunted. I live to outwit the Hunters for another day. To survive until I die with honor. But that will not be my fate."

The Bandi were tight-lipped as to how Farpoint Station's markets could provide anything and everything a visitor might want.
The Borg do not require sleep as humans know it, but they do spend time in regeneration alcoves to heal and recharge.
There is no escape from Tars Lamora, the brutal prison colony where slaves toil under the ironfisted rule of the Diviner.

"What kind of weirdo signs up for a job in outer space just to garden?"
—Ensign Beckett Mariner
There is no place more sacred to the Klingons than Boreth, where the followers of Kahless the Unforgettable await his return.
Borg surgical suites combine the most efficient aspects of a sickbay, machine shop, and brig.

"Whether you're buying, selling, or have to escape in a hurry, Denaxi Depot has what you need."
—*Lawmim Galactopedia*

"First time in a wormhole, Ensign? Keep us centered and off the ecliptic, or the quantum sheer will tear the cute right out of your baby pictures."
—Captain Hiram Gould

"The black hole seems to be inverting the wormhole, Captain. I suggest we relocate."
—Science Officer L'Tay
Within the gas giant, the Borg Queen could wait and plan.
The planet itself has no value. The more efficiently the Borg can extract what they need, the better.

"The outpost was not just destroyed. It's as though some great force just scooped it off the face of the planet."
—Lieutenant junior grade Worf
The hidden digital refuge of Unimatrix Zero proved that the Borg were not as harmonious as they preferred to believe.

"The entire region is filled with some kind of organic fluid. This isn't space. It's matter!"
—Lieutenant B'Elanna Torres

"My people encountered them a century ago. They destroyed our cities. Scattered my people throughout the Galaxy. They're called the Borg. Protect yourself, Captain, or they'll destroy you."
—Guinan

"The more difficult the task, the sweeter the victory."
—Commander William Riker
"Oh my. First impressions, right? First impressions are the most important?"

"My mom says two heads are better than one. Isn't that the Borg philosophy, too?"
—Naomi Wildman
"Designation: *Vor'cha*-class attack cruiser. Length: 481.32 meters. Hull: Duranium alloy. Threat assessment: 1.1%."
"It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness. That is life."

Not even the Borg can assimilate dust.
"*Cairo* to away team. We're getting a life sign, but that reactor leak is interfering with our scanners. You'll need to search each deck."

"Shields are down, but if we reroute warp plasma through the main deflector dish, we might just buy ourselves some time!"
—Lieutenant Kay Minamoto

"Captain, I believe the crew is de-evolving."
—Lieutenant Commander Data
In a moment, the *Enterprise*'s vast store of knowledge became just another piece of the vast Borg hive mind.
The Borg could see the color of her father's eyes, hear her son's laugh. The information would be analyzed for tactical advantage, then discarded.
Depending on the severity of its injuries, a drone will either receive a replacement arm or be fully recycled.
Nanoprobes begin the assimilation process, transforming flesh into crude implants.
Quantum torpedoes channel a matter/antimatter reaction four times the rate of a standard warhead through a zero-point initiator.

"Mister Worf, photon torpedoes. Maximum yield, full spread."
—Captain Jean-Luc Picard
Being a part of Starfleet is being a part of something bigger than yourself.

"Oh, stop! Back in the 21st Century, they sewed people up like they were torn trousers."
—Dr. Katherine Pulaski
"Eyes . . . in the dark . . . one moon circles . . ."
Dr. Noonien Soong built himself a pair of sons but proved a better scientist than a father. One became his legacy. The other, his killer.

"If you can't take a little bloody nose, maybe you ought to go back home and crawl under your bed. It's not safe out here! It's wondrous, with treasures to satiate desires both subtle and gross, but it's not for the timid."
The Prophets offer guidance through the divine Orbs. Not everyone listens.

"On its journey back, it amassed so much knowledge, it achieved consciousness itself. It became a living thing."
—Captain James T. Kirk

"Even in the darkest moments, you can always find something that'll make you smile."

The people of Kataan had been gone a thousand years. If one person remembered who they were and how they lived, then they'll have found life again.
The endless need for warp-enabling dilithium means even in the 24th Century, mining is a massive galactic industry.
The Eymorgs' underground complex on Sigma Draconis VI required a computer more advanced than anything they had ever built, a computer that only nature could craft.
Ocular implants feed a constant stream of subspace signals into the brain via the optic nerve.

"Actually, 'warp core' is a misnomer. It is technically a generator, but it's not a warp field generator. For some reason, 'deuterium/anti-deuterium intermix reactor' never caught on. Funny, right?"
—Lieutenant junior grade Sam Rutherford
Dilithium crystals provide critical regulation within a warp core, refining a deadly explosion into a constant stream of high-energy plasma.
Tools are extraneous. If a drone is incapable of a task, it must be upgraded.

"It's a human vice you might want to try one day. Keeps you sharp."
—Captain Kathryn Janeway

"If being human is not simply a matter of being born flesh and blood, if it is instead a way of thinking, acting, and feeling, then I am hopeful that one day I will discover my own humanity."
—Lieutenant Commander Data

"In their collective state, the Borg are utterly without mercy—driven by one will alone, the will to conquer. They are beyond redemption, beyond reason."
—Captain Jean-Luc Picard
The privilege of noble Houses, Klingon baldrics display family crests and medals.
IDIC—Infinite Diversity in Infinite Combinations—is a cornerstone of Vulcan philosophy.

"I have an ultimate storage capacity of eight hundred quadrillion bits. My total linear computational speed has been rated at sixty trillion operations per second."
—Lieutenant Commander Data
The most important element of a Borg's cybernetic array, the cortical node regulates and coordinates all other technological and biological functions.

"Expertise aplenty," Mister Scott confirmed. "But we'll see if they've got the heart."

"I've become romantically involved with a hologram inside Fair Haven. You know the story: Girl meets boy. Girl modifies boy's subroutines."
—Captain Kathryn Janeway

"I cannot describe the Great Link to you, Odo. It is like becoming the ocean—a perfect infinity."
—Female Changeling
Federation worlds house endless diversity, bound by a simple truth: we are better together.

"Starting to like this chair. It's feeling like a little piece of home we're carrying to the edge of the universe."
—Captain Jonathan Archer

"I'm a teacher. My responsibility is to expose my students to knowledge, not hide it from them."
—Keiko O'Brien

—Dr. Leonard McCoy

"Your death is too . . . easy. I find this unsatisfying."
—Armus

"I didn't mean to say that the *Enterprise* should be hauling garbage. I meant to say that it should be hauled away *as* garbage!"
—Korax, officer of the *I.K.S. Gr'oth*

"Dinosaurs pick up scents from miles away. We're here to observe and document, not interact."
—Sarah Harding

"Remember-viable embryos. They're no use to us if they don't survive."
—Lewis Dodgson
Once you have ascended to the highest temple of Orazca, the power of the Immortal Sun is yours to wield forever.

"If these sensors are working . . . we're on the other side of the Galaxy."
—Ensign Harry Kim
The automatons prepared entire colonies, unaware that a nova had consumed their makers' world.
There are no dead. Only raw materials.
There is no such thing as a single Borg.
"We all joined Starfleet to dive headfirst into the unknown."
"Engage!"

"If we're going to be damned, let's be damned for what we really are."
—Captain Jean-Luc Picard
The elegance of the Borg lies in how readily they integrate other species' solutions.
The iron hand of mercy rendered grief, remorse, loss, and fear all irrelevant.
"Confidence is faith in oneself. It can't easily be given by another."
The DOT-7s are designed to make repairs in any conditions too dangerous for humanoids.
"Damn. Where are the calluses we doctors are supposed to grow over our feelings?"
"What is this, the Dark Ages?!"

"Stop whining. Sto-Vo-Kor will be there later."
"Resistance is *not* futile."
"I am hologram Janeway, your training advisor for exploring the greater Galaxy. On behalf of Starfleet, welcome aboard."

"The holodeck safeties are still engaged, right?"
—Ensign Kei

faces.f: "The confinement beam subsystems check out, so do the phase transition coils."
Sometimes, hope is a choice.
The obedience of a Vulcan *sehlat* makes it a logical choice for a family pet. Some humans, facing six-inch fangs, question that logic.
"I have the utmost confidence in your ability to perform the impossible."
Each drone is defined by its role, but even authority provides no individual self. A brain is more useful than a toe, but neither is the body whole.
So advanced in thought and being, the Organians have no need for corporeal form.
"I don't believe this was a fair test of my command abilities."
Deflector shields use intense graviton fields to create a "solid" surface from nothing at all.
Although she was a Kelpien, a prey species, she feared no predator once behind the controls.
"Oh my."
"Kouassi to bridge. Captain, the intruders look like Starfleet, but their combadge is different. It's . . . a dagger through a planet?"

"In our next action, we can risk neither miscalculation nor error."
—Captain James T. Kirk

"They are detestable creatures."
—Lieutenant Commander Worf
"Starfleet is not a perfect organization, but it strives to be. And I believe it could be."
"Freedom is irrelevant. Self-determination is irrelevant. You must comply."
While the Prime Directive doesn't allow the Federation to interfere with pre-warp societies, it can learn from them.
Various sapient whale species serve in Starfleet as navigators, scientists, and explorers.

"She has an illusion, and you have reality. May you find your way as pleasant."
—The Keeper, magistrate of Talos IV

"Does Data have a soul? I don't know that he has. I don't know that I have. But I have got to give him the freedom to explore that question himself."
—Captain Phillipa Louvois
Neutrino spectrometry and quark resonance scans formed the foundation of Starfleet sensor tech, but active subspace flux analysis changed the game.
"You're too late. We are everywhere."
"Beam us up! BEAM US UP!"
"I took naturally to navigation, sir. After all, Russia invented the map."
The ionized gasses of the Mutara Nebula wreaked havoc with sensors and shielding.
For the briefest of moments, Spock felt fear. Not of the rabbit, but that the universe could let it exist without logical cause.
"Whatever they say, you have to respond in kind. Otherwise they'll take offense."
George and Gracie escaped extinction, and in the process, saved Earth.

"My alter ego, so to speak. You must admit, he's effective. You would never have been frightened by me."
—Balok
"Awesome. I know. I built them."
"Reasoning from the general to the specific. Is that not the very definition of deduction? Is that not the way Sherlock Holmes worked?"
"There's no way the computer can compensate for the human factor, the . . . the intuition, the experience."
"Okay, new plan!"
"Insufficient facts always invites danger."
She's fluent in thirty-seven languages and infinitely more insightful than a universal translator.
Some gestures are universal.
A resourceful crew can solve most any problem with elbow grease and dilithium.
Vulcans practice martial arts as a meditative exercise, though their physical aspects are sometimes useful.

faces.f: "And you people, you're all . . . astronauts on some kind of star trek."
The Vagrans cast off their evil, and it coalesced into a singular will.

"We have analyzed your defensive capabilities as being unable to withstand us. If you defend yourselves, you will be punished."
—The Borg

Peace through superior firepower.
—Minosian motto, pre-extinction
"Your tongue is as sharp as a warrior's! Let's see if your blade is as well!"
"I will rest when my blade knows vengeance."
Klingons who challenge the High Council are denied the right of personal combat. They must select a second—a *cha'DIch*—to defend them.
"You will be assimilated."
"I am eager to know if his blood runs as readily as his ship."
Perfection is not nurtured. It is created.
"I never tell the truth because I don't believe there is such a thing. That's why I prefer the straight-line simplicity of cutting cloth."
"The Federation is a social experiment doomed to failure. Childish idealism."
"Be honest, Captain. Warrior to warrior. You do prefer it this way, don't you? As it was meant to be. No peace in our time."
"Your choices have determined your fate."

There are no old warriors.
—Klingon proverb
"You always know what to expect when you do business with the Ferengi."

"How can we be powerful enough to wipe out a planet and still be so helpless?"
—Dr. Leonard McCoy
"Consensus achieved. Disseminating."
Saving Neelix and Tuvok meant destroying the person they'd become.

faces.f: It took masterful insight to lie with the Prophets' own words.
"Surely, I have made my meaning plain. I mean to avenge myself upon you, Admiral."
"Your resistance is wasted energy, and in time you'll wish you hadn't wasted it."

"From this time forward, you will service us."
—Locutus of Borg

"When they decide to come, they're going to come in force. They don't do anything piecemeal."
—Guinan
The Vau N'Akat created the Watchers to observe and the Drednoks to enforce.
After the collapse of their civilization, the people of M-113 became little more than predators, but they never abandoned their need for love.
Her mother shouldn't have existed, and young Sela ensured she did not.
"There we were at the K-7 cantina. Kirk's savage crew breathing down our necks. Their tribbles with fangs as sharp as a *mek'leth*."
"I don't understand how you can be so mistaken."
